amount of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

sentences.text: That on 15.08.2024 at about 1.50 PM., in 5th cross, MCECH Layout, wherein petitioner was sitting in the Auto beg. Reg. No.KA-03-AH-2796 by the side of the road, wherein the driver of Car bearing Reg No.KA-41-N-5437 drove it, with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Auto and caused accident,
in the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

He was shifted to the Prolife Multi specialty Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for the accidental injuries sustained by him and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/-.
Petitioner states that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to perform his work as earlier.
Prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and he is aged about 31 years and he was auto driver by profession and thereby he was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
Further petitioner stated that the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.98/2024 against the driver of the offending vehicle as the accident occurred due to his negligence.
Respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle, she insured her vehicle with the respondent No.1 and they are jointly liable to pay the compensation with interest.
He prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.

3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, they appeared through counsel and respondent No.1 filed vakalath and written statement and respondent No.2 has not chosen to file the written statement.
Respondent No.1 contended that the insured has violated the policy conditions and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
4. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked 16 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 16 and he is fully cross examined.
Respondent No.1 examined its legal manager as RW-1 and marked 2 documents which are Ex.R1 and 2 and she is fully cross examined.
5. I have heard the arguments for the counsels appearing for both the sides and I have perused the entire record.

Counsel appearing for respondent No.1 has relied on the New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
Vs Bibi Nafisa MFA No.7683/2014 C/w MFA No.54/2020- the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka order dated 28.05.2024.
6.

sentences.text:
On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 15.08.2024 at about 1.50 PM., in 5th cross,
MCECH Layout, petitioner was sitting in his Auto beg. Reg. No.KA-03-AH-2796 by the side of the road, wherein the driver of Car bearing Reg No.KA-41-N-5437 drove it,
with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Auto and caused accident, in the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition ?

Naveenkumar N vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98693435/
2 2.

entities.text: Naveenkumar N vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether respondent no.1 proves that the insured has violated the policy conditions as contended in the written statement ?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4.
What order or award?

7. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issues no.1: In the affirmative,
 Issues no.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issues No.3: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 8. Point No.1 & 2 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.
Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, police intimation,
mahazar, sketch, IMV request, final report, Notice U/s 133 of MV Act and reply notice which are at Ex.P.1 to 11.
9.

On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that one Bharath s/o Prabhu, aged about 13 years was the driver of the offending vehicle and the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving.
Ex.P.11 is the reply notice given by the Respondent No.2 to the notice issued by the police under section 133 of M.V.Act.

It reveals that, her son Bharat was the driver of the offending vehicle and he was having no valid and effective driving license and the policy of the offending vehicle was in force as on the date of the accident.

The final report which is at Ex.P9 is filed after investigation and it is the prima-facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and disbelieved.
10. Petitioner has tender the wound certificate as per Ex.P.6, discharge summaries as per Ex.P14.
The aforesaid documents shows that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injures that is right shoulder clavicle fracture, left shoulder and wrist and lower lip laceration injuries.
It also true that the surgery was done to the Petitioner for the aforesaid lacerated wound.
Petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 4 days in prolife multi specialty hospital and he has incurred medical expesnes of Rs.50,700/- as per Ex.P.14.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

sentences.text:
Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, Medicines,
Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
11.
Petitioner took treatment at Prolife multi specialty Hospital, Bangalore.
He has tendered the wound certificate, discharge summary and medical bills and reports along with the related documents.
On perusal of the same it is apparent that, petitioner has incurred Rs.50,700/- towards actual medical expenses.
Evidently there is no material to disbelieve the medical bills.

Accordingly,
the wound certificate, discharge summary and the medical bills issued form the hospital have to be accepted.

Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment for 4 days, for attendant charges,
transportation, nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses.
Petitioner has not examined the treated doctors or whispered the details of his functional disability.
Therefore in addition to the actual medical expenses of Rs.50,700/- I award Rs.10,000/-.
In total petitioner is entitled for Rs.60,700/- compensation under this head.
12. Patiently petitioner has not substantiated the nature of income.

Accident took place in the year 2024, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2024 is Rs.16,500/-,
and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least 1 month he has lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.16,500/- as compensation under this head.

II. NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:(General Damages) (IV) Damages for Pain & sufferings and Trauma as a consequence of the injuries :-
13.
The petitioner has undergone the pain and sufferings during the accident and during the rehabilitation period, therefore I award Rs.10,000/- as compensation under this head.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
14.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for him before accident.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- as compensation under this head.
15. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 Sl Particulars Amount  No.
 1 Towards medical expenses Rs.60,700/-
 2 Loss of income during laid up period Rs.16,500/-
 2 pain & sufferings Rs.10,000/-
 3 loss of amenities Rs.20,000/-

sentences.text: Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
17. Liability:
The respondent no.1 is the insurer of offending vehicle and respondent no.2 is the insured and owner of the offending vehicle.

The insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid as on the date of the incident and driver of the offending vehicle is not having valid DL as on the date of the accident and admittedly he was the minor as on the date of the accident.

Accordingly insurer has successfully plead and proved the fact that the respondent no.2 has violated/ breach the policy condition that is she knowingly and consciously handed over the offending vehicle and permitted/allowed the driver of the offending vehicle to drive the same with out valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident and it is the sole reason for the accident.
Add to it considering the facts and attending circumstance, apparently there is the clear breach of the policy condition by the insurer and it is the fundamental cause for the accident.
Accordingly the liability can not be attached to the insurer.
Inasmuch respondent no.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 & 2 in the affirmative and Issue No.3 in partly affirmative.
18. Issue No.4:

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.,1,07,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.
After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioner is permitted to withdraw entire compensation amount with interest.
Petitioner has to comply the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020, while withdrawing the compensation amount with interest.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
